risk_register.description: If technology stack for API gateway is not selected or team lacks direct experience with chosen stack, then Phase 2 implementation will require spike activities and learning curve, extending timeline by 2-3 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Open question priority 1 states: 'Does the 4-engineer team have direct experience with the chosen stack?' No stack or experience level mentioned in brief.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct technology stack selection workshop in week 1; confirm team experience with chosen framework (Go, Node.js, Python, etc.); allocate 3-5 days spike for proof-of-concept if stack is unfamiliar.
risk_register.contingency: If team lacks experience, hire external consultant for 2-week embedded mentoring during Phase 2, or extend timeline by 2-3 weeks for self-directed learning.

risk_register.description: If microservice inventory is dynamic (services scale up/down or join/leave mesh) rather than static, then gateway design must include service discovery integration (Consul, Eureka), adding 2-3 weeks and increasing complexity from TYPE_A to TYPE_D.
risk_register.trigger: Open question priority 2 states: 'Is the service inventory static or dynamic?' Assumption A2 assumes static list, but brief does not confirm this.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm service inventory scope in week 1 kickoff; if dynamic, allocate Phase 2 spike (3-5 days) to evaluate service discovery frameworks; document decision in design spec.
risk_register.contingency: If dynamic discovery required mid-project, descope advanced load balancing (UC5) or extend Phase 2 by 2 weeks for service registry integration and testing.

risk_register.description: If authentication/authorization implementation requires custom credential system instead of industry-standard OAuth 2.0 or JWT, then design, implementation, and security audit timeline extends 4-6 weeks, exceeding 4-month deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Open question priority 3 states: 'What is the authentication/authorization implementation standard?' Assumption A1 assumes OAuth 2.0/JWT, but brief does not confirm; custom auth would be a hard constraint violation.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm authentication standard (OAuth 2.0, JWT, mTLS) with stakeholders in week 1; if OAuth 2.0/JWT, verify Authentication Service (A5) is already deployed and accessible; document in design spec.
risk_register.contingency: If custom auth required, escalate to stakeholder for scope negotiation; either descope advanced features (canary routing, weighted load balancing) or extend timeline to 5-6 months.

risk_register.description: If Product Owner is not assigned or unavailable for sprint planning and backlog refinement, then Hybrid SDLC phase gates cannot be executed; Phase 2 kickoff is blocked.
risk_register.trigger: Open question priority 4 states: 'Who is the Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization?' No PO named in brief or project plan.
risk_register.mitigation: Assign Product Owner before Phase 1 kickoff; confirm availability for 4-6 hours/week sprint planning, backlog refinement, and stakeholder communication; document in RACI matrix.
risk_register.contingency: If PO unavailable, escalate to project sponsor for interim decision-making authority; establish weekly steering committee to unblock scope decisions.

risk_register.description: If expected request volume (RPS), concurrent user count, and SLA targets are not defined, then infrastructure sizing, load balancing algorithm choice, and caching strategy cannot be validated; Phase 3 testing may reveal performance gaps requiring re-architecture.
risk_register.trigger: Open question priority 5 states: 'What is the expected request volume (RPS), concurrent user count, and SLA for gateway availability and response latency?' No performance targets in brief or constraints.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct performance requirements workshop in week 1; define RPS, concurrent user count, latency SLA, and availability target; document in NFR specification; allocate Phase 2 spike (3-5 days) for load testing framework setup.
risk_register.contingency: If performance targets discovered late in Phase 3, conduct load testing; if targets unmet, descope features (advanced logging, detailed metrics) or extend Phase 3 by 1-2 weeks for optimization.

risk_register.description: If compliance or audit requirements (SOC2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) mandate request log retention, encryption, or access controls beyond 30-day default, then data retention architecture and cost model change; Phase 3 may require re-work for audit trail implementation.
risk_register.trigger: Open question priority 6 states: 'Are there compliance or audit requirements?' Brief does not mention compliance drivers; assumption A4 assumes 30-day retention without compliance mandate.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm compliance requirements (SOC2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, audit trail) with stakeholders and legal in week 1; if required, allocate Phase 2 spike (3-5 days) for data warehouse integration design; document in NFR specification.
risk_register.contingency: If compliance requirements discovered in Phase 2, evaluate data warehouse integration (BigQuery, Snowflake) or extend Phase 3 by 1-2 weeks for audit trail implementation and testing.

risk_register.description: If Authentication Service (A5) is not already deployed or accessible, then gateway cannot validate credentials; UC2 (Authenticate Request) cannot be tested or deployed until A5 is available.
risk_register.trigger: Assumption A1 assumes 'Authentication Service (A5 in use case model) already deployed'; brief does not confirm A5 exists or is accessible.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm Authentication Service deployment status and API contract in week 1; if not deployed, coordinate with A5 team for Phase 1 deployment; document API specification and test credentials.
risk_register.contingency: If A5 unavailable, mock Authentication Service in Phase 2 for development; coordinate with A5 team for integration testing in Phase 3; extend Phase 3 by 3-5 days for integration validation.

risk_register.description: If load balancing strategy (round-robin, least-connections, weighted routing, canary) is not confirmed, then Phase 2 design will require re-work if stakeholder expectations differ from assumption A3 (round-robin); adds 1-2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Assumption A3 assumes 'round-robin or least-connections'; brief lists 'load balancing' as requirement but does not specify algorithm or traffic shaping needs.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm load balancing strategy and traffic shaping requirements in week 1 design workshop; document in architecture specification; validate against service instance topology.
risk_register.contingency: If weighted routing or canary deployment required mid-Phase 2, descope advanced monitoring (UC7 detailed metrics) or extend Phase 2 by 1 week for algorithm implementation and testing.

risk_register.description: If any critical path role (Backend Developer, QA Engineer) becomes unavailable or is shared with competing projects, then zero-slack tasks (T1, T2, T5, T8, T11, T14, T17, T20, T23) will slip, delaying project completion beyond 4-month deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Project plan states: 'Backend Developer and QA Engineer must be dedicated (not shared) across all phases.' Brief does not confirm team is fully allocated or protected from competing priorities.
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from resource manager that Backend Developer and QA Engineer are 100% allocated to this project for 16 weeks; document in project charter; establish weekly resource status check.
risk_register.contingency: If resource contention occurs, escalate to project sponsor for priority negotiation; identify backup Backend Developer and QA Engineer; if unavailable, extend timeline by 2-3 weeks per resource loss.

risk_register.description: If stakeholder scope approval is not formally documented in writing, then scope creep risk increases; Phase 2 backlog refinement may reveal conflicting expectations on UC5 (Load Balance Request) or UC7 (Monitor Gateway Health) complexity.
risk_register.trigger: Brief does not mention formal written scope sign-off from stakeholders; success definition is stated but not confirmed as approved by all stakeholders.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct scope sign-off meeting in week 1; obtain written approval (email or signature) from all stakeholders on use case list, success criteria, and out-of-scope items (e.g., no canary routing, no advanced metrics); document in project charter.
risk_register.contingency: If scope disputes arise in Phase 2, convene change control board; evaluate impact on timeline and budget; document decision and communicate to all stakeholders.

risk_register.description: If request logging implementation does not account for high-volume API traffic, then logging service may become a bottleneck; UC4 (Log API Call) performance may degrade gateway throughput.
risk_register.trigger: Brief specifies 'request logging for all API calls' but does not define expected volume or logging latency SLA; open question priority 5 asks for RPS but does not address logging overhead.
risk_register.mitigation: Define logging latency SLA (e.g., <10ms per log write) in week 1 NFR specification; allocate Phase 2 spike (3-5 days) for logging framework evaluation (async queues, batching); conduct load testing in Phase 3.
risk_register.contingency: If logging becomes bottleneck in Phase 3 testing, implement async logging with message queue (Kafka, RabbitMQ) or extend Phase 3 by 3-5 days for optimization.

risk_register.description: If API versioning strategy (header-based, path-based, or content negotiation) is not confirmed, then UC6 (Support API Versioning) implementation will require re-work if stakeholder expectations differ from design assumption.
risk_register.trigger: Brief lists 'API versioning' as use case but does not specify versioning strategy; no design assumption documented for UC6.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm API versioning strategy in week 1 design workshop; document in architecture specification; validate against existing microservice versioning practices.
risk_register.contingency: If versioning strategy changes mid-Phase 2, update routing logic and test cases; if significant re-work required, extend Phase 2 by 3-5 days.

risk_register.description: If microservices do not expose consistent API contracts or documentation, then gateway routing logic will require custom adapters or transformation logic; UC1 (Route API Request) implementation extends by 1-2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Brief states 'Multiple services with inconsistent APIs' as trigger; brief does not confirm API contracts are documented or standardized.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct API contract discovery workshop in week 1; document all microservice endpoints, request/response schemas, and error codes; identify inconsistencies and standardization opportunities; allocate Phase 2 spike (3-5 days) for adapter design if needed.
risk_register.contingency: If microservices lack documentation, allocate Phase 2 time for reverse-engineering API contracts; if significant adaptation required, extend Phase 2 by 1-2 weeks.

risk_register.description: If team size (4 engineers) is insufficient for parallel development of UC1-UC7 across 4 phases, then critical path tasks will be serialized; timeline may slip beyond 16 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Brief states 'team size 4' with no role breakdown or seniority; project plan shows 9 zero-slack tasks requiring dedicated Backend Developer and QA Engineer; Frontend Developer has 3-5 days slack.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm team composition (Backend, QA, Frontend, DevOps/Infra roles) in week 1; validate skill matrix against use case complexity; if gaps exist, allocate mentoring or hire contractor for 4-6 weeks.
risk_register.contingency: If team capacity insufficient, descope UC7 (Monitor Gateway Health) advanced metrics or extend Phase 2 by 1-2 weeks for parallel development.

risk_register.description: If rate limiting algorithm (token bucket, sliding window, fixed window) is not specified, then UC3 (Apply Rate Limiting) implementation will require design decision; may not align with microservice rate limiting policies.
risk_register.trigger: Brief lists 'rate limiting' as requirement but does not specify algorithm or per-client vs. per-endpoint granularity.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm rate limiting requirements in week 1 design workshop; document algorithm choice, granularity, and enforcement policy; validate against existing microservice rate limiting.
risk_register.contingency: If rate limiting policy changes mid-Phase 2, update algorithm and test cases; if significant re-work required, extend Phase 2 by 2-3 days.
